notes.title: Two ways to say a color
notes.text: Many colors are adjectives (빨갛다 → 빨간 옷 "red clothes", 하얗다 → 하얀 옷) and also nouns with 색 "color" (빨간색, 하얀색). Black has two everyday nouns: 까만색 and 검정색. Green is 초록색 in daily talk and 녹색 in more formal words like 녹차 "green tea".

lessons.goal: Try on clothes, ask the price, and pay.

notes.title: Shopping phrases
notes.text: 입어 봐도 돼요? (May I try it on?) · 다른 색 있어요? (Do you have another color?) · 좀 깎아 주세요 (Please give me a discount — markets only!) · 교환돼요? / 환불돼요? (Can I exchange / get a refund?). Stores call customers 고객님 or 손님.

notes.title: Wearing verbs
notes.text: Korean uses different verbs for "wear": 입다 (clothes), 신다 (shoes, socks), 쓰다 (hats, glasses), 끼다 (rings, gloves), 매다 (ties, belts), 메다 (a bag on the shoulder), 하다 (accessories in general — 목걸이를 하다).

notes.title: Weight talk
notes.text: 살이 찌다 = gain weight, 살이 빠지다 = lose weight (it "falls out"), 살을 빼다 = lose weight on purpose. Koreans often comment on weight more openly than Americans — 살 빠졌네! is usually meant as a compliment. You can answer lightly: 그래요? 감사해요.

notes.title: Poetic colors
notes.text: Besides everyday 빨갛다 / 파랗다 / 하얗다 / 까맣다, Korean has older, literary color words: 붉다 (red), 푸르다 (blue-green — the sky, the sea, and young leaves), 희다 (white), 검다 (black). You'll meet them in songs, poems, and webtoon titles. 푸르다 covers both blue and green, like 푸른 하늘 and 푸른 산.
